canonical_topic: Roles in a regulated electricity grid
definition: In regulated markets, one entity typically performs all four core grid functions (generation, transmission, distribution, retail sale), usually as a government-sanctioned monopoly, though ownership models vary by type of sponsor.
core_idea: Regulated-market utilities come in several forms depending on ownership: investor-backed integrated utilities, government-owned munis, not-for-profit rural co-ops, and federally owned utilities often tied to hydroelectric generation.
key_points: Integrated utility: a regulated monopoly owning generation, transmission, and distribution assets together.
Municipally owned utility (muni): publicly owned by a local government.
Co-operative (co-op): not-for-profit, typically serving rural areas that are unprofitable for traditional utilities to serve.
Federally owned utility: a government entity, often involving hydroelectric generation, authorized to buy, sell, and distribute power.
relationships: Contrasts with the unbundled roles (merchant generator, wires company, LSE, POLR) found in deregulated markets.
